title: Checker verdict
description: A checker's verdict on one guild task, written as JSON (the record of record) and rendered to a Markdown sibling for humans. Structured-output-safe by construction: no if/then, no $dynamicRef, no unevaluatedProperties, only the conservative keyword set (type, properties, required, items, enum, additionalProperties) — a second checker family writes this shape via strict vendor structured-output modes, which cannot evaluate conditionals. All nine properties are required, with none marked optional: OpenAI's strict structured-output mode (the mode `codex exec --output-schema` uses) rejects a schema that leaves any key out of `required` outright, so `duration_ms` and `cost_usd` are typed nullable (`["integer", "null"]` and `["number", "null"]`) instead — a checker that doesn't know a wall-clock time or cost emits `null` for it, meaning unreported, never a fabricated 0, the same convention `vendor-call.schema.json` uses for its own nullable fields. Two further compromises this implies: (1) the three semantic rules a conditional would normally express here — a fail verdict must carry at least one finding, every finding's evidence must be non-empty, and a pass verdict must carry no blocker or major finding — are enforced by validate-verdict.py instead of by this schema; (2) 'blocked' is not a third flavor of outcome alongside pass/fail, it carries the guild's old ERROR semantics (the check itself couldn't complete — script crashed, tool unreachable, vendor quota hit) and does not count against the worker's retry budget.

task_id.description: The task this verdict checks, e.g. "T-001".

checker.description: The checker agent that produced this verdict, e.g. "checker-judgment".

vendor.description: The model vendor that ran the check, e.g. "anthropic".

model.description: The model that ran the check, e.g. "claude-opus-4".

clause_id.description: The constitution clause this finding is about, e.g. "C-1".

severity.description: The impact of the defect this finding reports. "blocker" means the artifact must not ship as it stands; "major" a real defect that has to be fixed; "minor" a small one worth naming; "info" no defect at all, the finding records a clause being satisfied. A clause's own severity in the constitution is the cost of VIOLATING it, not the label for every finding about it: a finding confirming that a blocker-severity clause is met is "info". A pass verdict therefore carries only "info" and "minor" findings, since "blocker" and "major" both assert a defect and contradict a verdict saying every cited clause is satisfied.

description.description: One sentence stating the defect or the clause being satisfied.

evidence.description: A file path plus line range (e.g. "foo.py:12-18"), or a command-output excerpt.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock duration of the check, in milliseconds, or null if unreported — never a fabricated 0.

cost_usd.description: The check's cost in US dollars, or null if unreported — never a fabricated 0.
